items.title: Context-Dependent Clinical Narrative Signals of Renal Function Deterioration in Cross-Language Settings: Retrospective Multicohort Study.
items.abstract: Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) classifies chronic kidney disease (CKD) using categories based on both glomerular filtration rate and albuminuria. Structured measures remain essential but may not capture contextual clinical concerns documented in narrative records. This study examined whether text-derived clinical-status language features in clinician notes were associated with deterioration in renal function in independent Greek- and English-language clinical cohorts. We retrospectively analyzed a Greek general-nephrology cohort (314 patients; 10,306 estimated glomerular filtration rate [eGFR] measurements) and an independent English-language Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) replication cohort. The Greek primary analysis used a linear mixed effects model over a follow-up period of up to 1797 days. The MIMIC-IV primary analysis used a 90-day, patient-level fixed-horizon competing-outcome model (N=87,533). Separate analyses of Greek and MIMIC-IV data evaluated discrimination, calibration, and sensitivity to alternative feature specifications. In the Greek cohort, a 1-SD higher negativity was associated with lower eGFR ( β =-3.273 mL/min/1.73 m², 95% CI -5.049 to -1.498; P β =-1.324, 95% CI -2.553 to -0.096; P =.035). In MIMIC-IV, a 1-SD higher negative-vs-reassuring polarity contrast was associated with renal deterioration (relative risk ratio [RRR]=1.090, 95% CI 1.070-1.110; P <.001). Within eGFR G categories, polarity-score areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.506 to 0.552 using discharge eGFR and 0.518 to 0.534 using the worst observed eGFR. Discrimination for renal deterioration remained modest (one-vs-rest AUC=0.6134, 95% CI 0.6092-0.6175), and adding both natural language processing (NLP) features to the clinical model increased AUC by only 0.0018 (95% CI 0.0010-0.0025). Independently constructed clinical-language measures were associated with renal function deterioration across two languages and health care settings. The findings support cross-language replication of an association signal, not formal external validation, measurement equivalence, or clinically useful stand-alone prediction.

items.title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.
items.abstract: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm 2 , and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

items.title: Molecular basis of quorum-sensing signal transduction by CqsS and its inhibition by CqsA, the autoinducer synthase.
items.abstract: Vibrio bacteria possess multiple quorum-sensing systems, each of which conveys information into the cell concerning the cell density and species composition of the vicinal community. Germane to the present work is the CqsA-CqsS quorum-sensing pathway that vibrios use for intragenus communication. CqsA is the synthase for the autoinducer ( S )-3-hydroxytridecan-4-one (CAI-1), and CqsS, a bifunctional two-component kinase-phosphatase, is the CAI-1 receptor. Here, we determine the cryo-EM structures of the full-length Vibrio harveyi CqsS dimer in the apo- and ATPγS-bound states. Our structures reveal the molecular basis for the initiation of the phosphorylation cascade, which we support through biochemical and genetic analyses. Autophosphorylation of CqsS occurs in cis at the conserved histidine residue (H1), whereas phospho-transfer to the conserved aspartate residue (D1) in the C-terminal receiver domain occurs in trans . By coexpressing CqsS and CqsA to capture CqsS bound to CAI-1, we unexpectedly find a tight interaction between the CqsS intracellular domain and CqsA. In the complex, the CqsS H1 residues are positioned away from the catalytic cavity, and CqsS kinase activity is inhibited. Cryo-EM analysis, focused on the transmembrane domain of CqsS in this complex, reveals the presence of two CAI-1 molecules. CAI-1 binding induces an obvious movement of transmembrane helix 6, disrupting its extension into the cytosol, providing a structural basis for how CAI-1 binding in the periplasm is coupled to signal transduction into the cytoplasm. Together, our findings advance the understanding of CqsS-CAI-1-mediated quorum-sensing signal transduction, an activity that underpins the coordination of group behaviors in vibrios.

items.title: 2026 update on routine and special vaccinations in people with HIV.
items.abstract: Vaccinations are an important part of primary care for people with HIV (PWH). They protect against some sexually transmitted infections, and respiratory bacterial and viral infections. PWH are recommended to obtain influenza, COVID-19, herpes zoster (shingles), hepatitis B, meningococcal disease, mpox, and human papillomavirus vaccinations. Additionally, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices has released recommendations incorporating the newer formulations of pneumococcal pneumonia vaccines and respiratory syncytial virus vaccines. Considerations for the timing of vaccinations are described, including whether to delay vaccination until improvement of the immune status. Live vaccines (other than nonreplicating vaccines) are contraindicated for PWH with a CD4+ count below 200 cells/μL or uncontrolled HIV.

items.title: Active immunotherapy against IL-1β restores tissue repair under chronic inflammation.
items.abstract: Chronic inflammation driven by sustained interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β) signaling disrupts the resolution phase of tissue repair by orchestrating dysregulated immune activity. As a key upstream mediator, IL-1β prolongs the activation of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells and establishes an environment that prevents the transition to tissue repair. Here, we developed an active immunotherapy against IL-1β using the self-assembling peptide nanofiber Coil29, which elicits robust and specific IL-1β-targeted immune responses in both wild-type and diabetic mice, without inducing systemic immunosuppression. In a chronic wound model, the therapy accelerated re-epithelialization and enhanced overall tissue regeneration, outperforming anti-IL-1β monoclonal antibodies. This therapy suppressed macrophage activity, promoted their M2-like polarization, enhanced pro-healing cytokine secretion and enriched the injury site with anti-IL-1β antibodies. In vitro, we found that antibodies from immunized mice reprogrammed M1 macrophages toward an M2-like phenotype, suggesting that antibody-mediated modulation of IL-1β activity may drive the enhanced wound re-epithelization seen in immunized animals. Altogether, these findings highlight a targeted, regenerative therapy for the healing of chronic wounds.

items.title: Enablers and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination implementation among key stakeholders in Ethiopia: A qualitative study.
items.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective and lifesaving intervention against cervical cancer. However, achieving high, equitable, and sustainable uptake remains a significant challenge in low-resource settings, including Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the enablers and barriers to HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia. An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed in purposively selected settings representing diverse socio-ecological contexts (Afar, Amhara, Addis Ababa, and Dire Dawa). Six focus group discussions were conducted with adolescent girls (n = 14), parents of eligible adolescent girls (n = 14), and community representatives (n = 14). In addition, nineteen key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with healthcare providers, Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) coordinators, and technical advisors from governmental and non-governmental organizations. Data were analysed using a combined deductive-inductive content analysis guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0). Multiple interacting factors influenced HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia, categorised as enablers and barriers across community, health system, and policy levels. Enablers included the Perceived Vaccine Attributes and Delivery Adaptability, Supportive Policy and Multisectoral Strategic Partnerships, Socio-cultural and Belief-based Drivers, and Health System Readiness and Workforce Motivation. However, several barriers limited implementation, including Suspicions About Targeting 9-14-year-old Girls and Consent-related Administrative Obstacles, Pervasive Misinformation and Cognitive Resistance, Health System Resource Constraints and Coordination Gaps, Donor Dependency Risks and Financial Sustainability Concerns, and Structural Access Constraints and Equity Gaps. While policy shifts, external strategic partnerships, and frontline worker dedication have accelerated vaccine reach, the long-term sustainability of Ethiopia's HPV vaccination program remains constrained by multi-level barriers. Progress toward the global 2030 cervical cancer elimination targets requires trust-building risk-communication strategies to counter fertility myths, simplified consent procedures, targeted domestic resource mobilization, and context-specific delivery models tailored to underserved pastoralist and urban sub-populations.

items.title: Effects of Concomitant Medications on Clinical and Immunological Outcomes of Cancer Patients Treated With Oncolytic Adenoviruses.
items.abstract: Medication taken for other reasons than for the treatment of malignant disease, termed concomitant medication, is known to affect outcomes when used with immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and other oncological drugs. However, no research in humans has addressed the relationship between concomitant medications and efficacy of oncolytic adenovirus (OAd) therapy. We retrospectively collected medication history of 290 patients enrolled in the Advanced Therapy Access Program (ATAP), an individualized treatment program of OAds. We analyzed associations of different concomitant medications with overall survival and imaging response following therapy. Additionally, to provide further insights into mechanisms using tissue samples, we collected concomitant medication data, tumor transcriptomic data and serum proteomic data from recent Phase I clinical trials with OAd igrelimogene litadenorepvec (Ad5/3-E2F-d24-hTNF-IRES-hIL2, TILT-123). In ATAP, acetaminophen (paracetamol), opium alkaloids, anti-emetics, proton pump inhibitors, beta blockers, laxatives, and antidepressants use showed a statistical association with shorter overall survival. Use of lipid-modifying drugs (statins) and thyroid hormones showed a statistical association with better disease control in imaging. In clinical trials with TILT-123, beta blockers, anti-emetics, opioids, and benzodiazepines showed a statistical association with shorter overall survival, and lipid-modifying drugs and thyroid hormones showed a statistical association with improved disease control. Tumor transcriptomic and serum proteomic analysis showed varied temporal and locational effects on inflammatory response varying by drug class. The results provide the first human data suggesting that OAd therapy outcomes might be influenced by concomitant medications. Future studies on mechanisms of reported findings have the possibility of tailoring clinical use of OAds.

items.title: Modelling and analysis of infectious diseases considering vaccination, mutation and quarantine strategies.
items.abstract: From an experimental point of view, it is difficult to investigate the propagation mechanism of infectious disease and predict its trend. However, applying a nonlinear model offers a more straightforward and effective approach for analyzing transmission characteristics of infectious diseases. This paper proposes an SLVEIMQR dynamic model by dividing the population into susceptible (S), low-risk (L), vaccinated (V), exposed (E), infected (I), mutant (M), quarantined (Q) and recovered (R). The basic reproduction number and the equilibrium of the proposed model are computed, and the local asymptotic stability of the disease-free equilibrium is proved. Furthermore, the transcritical bifurcation at equilibrium and the sensitivity of key parameters are analyzed. To estimate the model parameters and predict the trend of infectious disease, the least squares method is applied by using epidemic data from different phases in Italy. The results show that the average relative errors of the model in the two prediction stages are 1.72% and 3.66%, respectively.

items.title: Exploring community pharmacists' preparedness for delivering HIV, hepatitis C, and syphilis point-of-care and dried blood spot testing in the APPROACH 2.0 study.
items.abstract: Rates of sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections (STBBIs) continue to rise in Canada. Expanding access to testing is a key national priority, and pharmacists represent an accessible point of care for STBBI testing services. While pharmacist-led STBBI testing has demonstrated feasibility and acceptability, pharmacists' preparedness to deliver point-of-care (POC) or dried blood spot (DBS) testing has not been well-described. This study explored pharmacists' self-perceived preparedness to offer STBBI testing as part of the APPROACH 2.0 study. Pharmacists who conducted at least 1 testing encounter as part of the APPROACH 2.0 study were invited to participate in virtual focus groups. Semi-structured focus group data were analyzed using deductive content analysis guided by a predefined coding framework. The study was reported in accordance with the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ). Six focus groups were conducted with 18 pharmacists. Three insights into self-perceived preparedness were identified: practical, psychosocial, and contextual preparedness. Practical preparedness was strengthened through hands-on training, repeated testing encounters, and overlap with existing pharmacy skills, though DBS posed greater challenges than POC testing. Psychosocial preparedness impacted patient recruitment and reactive results delivery, with pharmacists expressing ongoing emotional and communication challenges. Contextual preparedness was influenced by pharmacy workflow, appointment-based scheduling and team engagement. Pharmacists largely felt prepared to deliver STBBI testing, particularly when training incorporated simulation, repetition, and practice-based reinforcement. Addressing challenges related to DBS testing, reactive result delivery, and the pharmacy environment may further strengthen preparedness and support broader implementation of pharmacist-led STBBI testing services in Canada. Pharmacists' self-perceived preparedness to provide STBBI testing was shaped by practical skills, psychosocial confidence, and contextual factors. Targeted training, ongoing practice and supportive pharmacy environments may enhance preparedness and facilitate the sustainable integration of pharmacist-led STBBI testing services across Canada.

items.title: Divergent dependence on host gene sigma-1 receptor shapes hepatitis C and orthoflavivirus infection.
items.abstract: The Flaviviridae family encompasses major human pathogens, such as hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV). Despite shared genome organization and replication strategies, these viruses differ in host interactions, tissue tropism and replication dynamics, leading to distinct disease outcomes. Sigma-1 receptor (SIGMAR1) encodes an endoplasmic reticulum-associated protein that regulates lipid transport, autophagy and proteostasis. We previously showed that SIGMAR1 silencing reduces early HCV infection efficiency without affecting unrelated viruses. Here, we demonstrate that SIGMAR1 is rate-limiting for the formation of normal double-membrane vesicles (DMVs), the putative HCV replication compartments. In contrast, DENV and West Nile virus (WNV) RNA replication remained efficient following SIGMAR1 depletion, indicating a selective requirement for SIGMAR1 in HCV DMV formation. Notably, SIGMAR1 knockdown markedly impaired secretion of infectious DENV and WNV particles without reducing intracellular progeny, suggesting a role for SIGMAR1 in orthoflavivirus virion release. SIGMAR1 silencing also disrupted Golgi architecture and altered cellular detergent-resistant membrane composition, consistent with defects in vesicular trafficking. These findings identify SIGMAR1 as a host factor with distinct functions in the replication cycles of hepaciviruses and orthoflaviviruses and highlight its broader role in maintaining membrane organization required for efficient infection by Flaviviridae .

items.title: Prospective Evaluation of Hepatitis B Virus Reactivation in Cancer Patients Receiving Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors.
items.abstract: Data on hepatitis B virus reactivation (HBVr) during tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy remain limited. We prospectively enrolled patients with chronic or resolved HBV receiving TKIs for lung cancer or chronic myeloid leukemia at one Taiwanese center (January 2023-March 2025). HBV DNA and liver enzymes were monitored 12-weekly and HBsAg 24-weekly. HBVr was defined by AASLD criteria, with APASL and EASL definitions applied secondarily. Among 79 patients (20 HBsAg-positive, 59 resolved HBV), none received antiviral prophylaxis. Median follow-up was 42 weeks (IQR, 19-65). HBVr occurred in 7 (8.9%; 95% CI, 4.4%-17.2%): 5 HBsAg-positive (25.0%; 95% CI, 11.2%-46.9%), and 2 with resolved HBV (3.4%; 95% CI, 0.9%-11.5%). APASL and EASL definitions yielded 30.0% and 35.0% in HBsAg-positive patients, with no additional events in resolved HBV. No HBVr-associated hepatitis flare meeting the study definition was observed, although transient flares between assessments could not be excluded and deterioration in one fatal case was attributed clinically to sepsis. Median HBVr detection time was 19 weeks (IQR, 14-30). Week-48 Kaplan-Meier HBVr incidence was 37.5% (95% CI, 17.0%-69.5%) in HBsAg-positive and 5.6% (95% CI, 1.4%-21.2%) in resolved HBV (log-rank p < 0.001); Aalen-Johansen estimates were 28.3% (95% CI, 9.5%-50.9%) and 4.3% (95% CI, 0.8%-13.2%), respectively. In exploratory Firth-corrected regression, HBsAg positivity was associated with HBVr (HR, 6.95; 95% CI, 1.60-40.19), while osimertinib exposure was not. HBVr was common among HBsAg-positive patients and less common but not negligible among those with resolved HBV receiving TKIs.

items.title: Chronic Hepatitis B in the United States: Current Landscape, Unmet Needs and Future Directions.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection represents a major public health challenge in the US, with substantial unmet needs related to timely diagnosis, treatment, monitoring and disease management. This narrative review explores the CHB landscape in the US, including gaps in patient care, the evolving therapeutic landscape, the clinical utility of serological biomarkers to improve outcomes and the experiences of people living with hepatitis B (PLWHB). Hepatitis B remains underdiagnosed and undertreated in the US, and current efforts are insufficient to meet the associated World Health Organization 2030 elimination targets. Latest guidelines from the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases and the Infectious Diseases Society of America, representing a North American perspective, signify a shift towards expanded treatment eligibility criteria and shared decision-making. Nucleos(t)ide analogues (NAs) are the current standard of care in the US, but functional cure is rarely achieved with NAs alone. Novel finite therapies targeting functional cure, such as antisense oligonucleotides, small interfering RNAs, immune modulators and combination or sequential regimens, are under investigation. Because of the unpredictable, complex nature of CHB, biomarkers such as quantitative hepatitis B surface antigen offer prognostic value for treatment decisions and could help guide individualised CHB management. PLWHB experience psychological impacts and health-related concerns, including fear of transmission and hepatitis B virus-related complications. Opportunities for improvement of CHB management include increased screening and linkage to care, development of more treatments targeting functional cure, adoption of serological biomarkers to inform treatment decisions and prioritising the lived experiences and preferences of PLWHB.

items.title: Use of Large Language Models for Automated Short-Answer Question Grading in Second-Cycle Medical Education: Performance and Consistency Evaluation Study.
items.abstract: Short-answer questions (SAQs) effectively assess higher-order reasoning skills in medical education but face challenges in scalability due to time-intensive manual grading and concerns about interrater reliability. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) may offer a solution through automated assessment. This study evaluated the performance and consistency of LLMs-ChatGPT, Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro-compared with those of human graders for SAQ grading in hepatology and gastroenterology. We retrospectively analyzed SAQs from hepatology and gastroenterology examinations at Sorbonne University, Paris, France (2023-2025). Three human evaluators (2 hepatogastroenterologists and 1 radiologist) independently graded all responses twice, with the majority consensus score serving as the reference standard. Six LLMs were evaluated: ChatGPT (GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, GPT-4o3, and GPT-5), Claude Sonnet 4, and Mistral Pro. Each LLM graded all responses twice using standardized prompts, including questions, model answers, grading guidelines, and scoring rubrics. Agreement was assessed using quadratic weighted kappa (QWK), Cohen κ, the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), and the mean absolute error (MAE) for interhuman, intrahuman, LLM-versus-human, and intramodel comparisons. A total of 902 student responses from 12 SAQs were included and analyzed. Interhuman grader agreement was almost perfect (QWK 0.90-0.92; ICC 0.90-0.92; MAE 0.05-0.07). Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3 demonstrated near-human-level performance when compared with the majority vote of human evaluators (Claude Sonnet 4: QWK 0.88-0.90; ICC 0.88-0.90; MAE 0.06-0.07 and GPT-4o3: QWK 0.82-0.89; ICC 0.82-0.89; MAE 0.07-0.09). GPT-5 showed substantial agreement (QWK 0.77-0.79). Mistral Pro and older ChatGPT versions performed poorly (QWK <0.63). Intramodel consistency was the highest for Claude Sonnet 4 (QWK 0.93), approaching the best human intrarater reliability. Agreement did not correlate with prompt design choices (number of examples or minimum word count). Advanced LLMs, particularly Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4o3, demonstrated near-human-level grading performance, supporting their potential use as assistive tools in SAQ grading. However, performance varied by model, and agreement alone does not ensure educational validity. Until broader multicenter validation is conducted across diverse domains, stakes, and question formats-along with safeguards for bias, privacy, and model drift-LLMs should augment rather than replace human faculty graders.

items.title: Local Therapy of Metastases in Colorectal Cancer: Utilization and Survival in a Nationwide Population.
items.abstract: Local therapy (LT) for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is recommended when eradicating all metastases is feasible. Although LT is widely used, its population-level impact remains unclear. This study aims to use real-world population-based data to assess LT utilization and survival trends in mCRC. Patients diagnosed with mCRC from 2010 to 2023 were included, using data from the Cancer Registry of Norway and the Norwegian Patient Registry. LT was defined as surgery, stereotactic radiotherapy (SRT), or ablation targeting liver, lung, or brain metastases. Outcomes were reported as median overall survival (OS) and 2-, 5-, and 10-year OS. The effect of the first versus last time period on survival was assessed using univariable and multivariable Cox regression. Among 64,112 CRC cases, 20,210 had mCRC. Of these, 21% received LT, 39% systemic therapy only, 12% other therapies, and 29% no therapy. Metastasectomy was the primary LT (87%), whereas SRT use was limited. LT use increased by 12% annually from 2010 to 2015 and then stabilized. The overall mCRC survival improved, with the 5-year OS increasing from 16% to 23% and the median OS from 15 to 18 months (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.89 to 0.95). No significant survival improvement was observed between time periods in the LT or systemic therapy only subgroups. The 5-year OS for patients receiving LT for liver, lung, and brain metastases was 50%, 62%, and 5%, respectively. LT utilization increased, with outcomes comparable with more selected populations. Survival in treatment subgroups remained stable over time, but improved in the overall mCRC population, suggesting that the population-level gains may reflect changes in treatment allocation rather than improvements within modalities.

items.title: Kinome profiling enabled development of a LATS1/2 inhibitor with wound healing potential.
items.abstract: System-level mapping of kinase inhibitors' polypharmacology can uncover opportunities for drug repurposing and identify starting points for medicinal chemistry campaigns aimed at novel targets. Here, we describe a large-scale profiling of 257 kinase inhibitors that revealed domains of promiscuity, a broad region of uninhibited targets and discrete pockets of selectivity. Focusing on a subcluster enriched for AGC group kinases and using the AKT inhibitor AT-7867 (an antiproliferative agent) as a starting point, we employed scaffold hopping and property-based optimization to discover NCGC-6782, a LATS1/2 inhibitor with robust proproliferative activity. In biochemical and cell-based assays, NCGC-6782 inhibited LATS1/2 activity, reduced YAP phosphorylation, and promoted rapid YAP nuclear translocation and transactivation of YAP-target genes. Kinome-wide profilings demonstrated good in vitro selectivity and exquisite chemoproteomic and kinetic selectivity. In vivo, NCGC-6782 exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic (PK) profiles following intraperitoneal (IP), intravenous (IV), or oral (PO) dosing, leading to rapid inhibition of YAP-phosphorylation in murine liver samples. Transcriptomics and proteomics following NCGC-6782 revealed upregulation of YAP-dependent genes (4 h) followed by activation of cell cycle programs (24 h). Consistently, NCGC-6782 accelerated proliferative regeneration in both cell-based and in vivo wound healing models of full-thickness excisional skin injury, significantly shortening wound-closure time without evidence of systemic toxicity. Altogether, we describe an optimized, potent, and selective LATS1/2 kinase inhibitor with desirable drug-like properties and broad potential for regenerative medicine applications following acute injury of nonproliferative, postmitotic tissues.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

items.title: Enhancing cell type deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics through incorporating multiple reference panels.
items.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) captures gene expression with spatial context but often at resolutions where each spatial location contains multiple cells. Deconvolution of cell-type proportions is therefore essential, yet existing methods typically rely on a single scRNA-seq reference, limiting accuracy when references are incomplete or mismatched especially in complex tissues. These limitations highlight the need for a framework that can integrate multiple references while leveraging spatial information. We introduce SWIMR (Spatially Weighted Integration for Multi-Reference deconvolution), a statistical framework that integrates multiple scRNA-seq references while accounting for spatial correlations. SWIMR models each spatial location as a weighted combination of references, with both cell-type proportions and reference weights varying across tissue locations. Across comprehensive simulations and diverse ST datasets, SWIMR consistently outperformed single-reference approaches. In developing human heart tissue, it recovered ground-truth cell-type compositions with the highest accuracy. In human lung and breast cancer, SWIMR delineated tumor, stromal, and immune compartments, uncovered tumor-adjacent populations, and detected cell type-specific spatially variable genes missed by other methods. In mouse embryo and liver cancer, it leveraged context-specific references to resolve organ-specific cell types and increase sensitivity for biologically relevant pathways. Together, these results establish SWIMR as a robust framework for multi-reference deconvolution in spatial transcriptomics.

items.title: The Modern Continuum of Care for Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Comprehensive Review.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the liver is its predominant site of metastatic spread; approximately half of patients with CRC develop colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). Management has shifted from largely palliative intent to a multidisciplinary strategy with curative potential. Complete resection offers a chance of cure, although long-term survival varies substantially with tumor biology, disease burden, and patient selection. This review summarizes advances in prognostic stratification, molecular profiling, and the evolving definition of resectability, together with surgical innovations including parenchymal-sparing and two-stage hepatectomy, portal vein embolization, associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS), liver venous deprivation, and minimally invasive approaches. We review conversion chemotherapy informed by the TRIBE, TRIBE2, CAIRO5, and PARADIGM trials, perioperative systemic therapy, and biomarker-directed agents for RAS wild-type, BRAF V600E-mutant, KRAS G12C-mutant, and HER2-amplified tumors, alongside immune checkpoint inhibition for microsatellite instability-high disease. Locoregional therapies, including thermal ablation, stereotactic radiotherapy, and selective internal radiation therapy, are discussed in light of the COLLISION and CLOCC trials. Finally, we consider emerging roles for circulating tumor DNA in minimal residual disease assessment and for liver transplantation in highly selected patients with unresectable disease (SECA, TransMet).
